Hint normalization via normalizeSkillName aligns before/after matching, including invalid-name entries matching undefined.

No new write paths or permission bypass; delegation-owner guard still relies on completedSkill with realpath/byte checks. Unmatched hints now yield unknown-call (fail-closed: owner not credited) rather than misattribution.

Rollback paths updated to per-session state and prune empty sessions. New MAX_PENDING_SESSIONS=256 LRU can evict an entire oldest session's pending state under >256 concurrent sessions; that fails closed (Task denied), and it is non-blocking. Unmatched synthetic entries remain queued until the 64-entry cap or session clear, which is bounded.

Test 3b would fail on the prior shift fallback (the delegation callID would be stolen, so the Task would be denied). The other-session-ok test would fail on the prior global 64-entry cap. No test covers the 256-session cap. That gap is minor.
Change is scoped to the two open P2 items. The session cap is a small added bound needed to keep per-session maps bounded. No unrelated scope.
In-memory state only; dispose and clearSessionPending reset fully; git revert restores the prior behavior.
No change to diagnostics. Unpaired calls surface as unknown-call IDs as before.
The 'per session' cap claim now holds, but it sits under an additional global 256-session bound that the claims don't mention. That is minor and not materially misleading.
Client-plumbing ownership pairing is now stricter: no cross-session or cross-skill callID theft. Behavior fails closed.
Tests stay self-contained with synthetic data. No packages/opencode-plugin contract rule is violated, and the delta needs no contract-file changes.

challenge_focus: Review delta for any P0/P1. Open items (verbatim): (1) P2 ccl-skills.ts:365: setBoundedPendingSkill evicts the oldest entry from one shared pendingSkills map, capped at 64 for all sessions combined. A busy or noisy session that opens 64 or more Skill calls without a matching after evicts another session's in-flight owner-skill load. That session's after then finds no pending entry, and its later Task is wrongly denied by the delegation-owner guard. The plan and evidence docs say the cap is per session. (2) P2 ccl-skills.ts:411: For a skill call with no callID, if the after hook's skillHint matches no queued entry (for example, the before hook had an invalid name), dequeueSyntheticCall falls back to queue.shift(). That takes another queued skill's synthetic callID. The later after for that other skill then gets the wrong ID or 'unknown-call', so its tool_result does not pair with its tool_use and its owner load is lost.
